title: Shot by ICE, Man Appears in Immigration Court With Bullet Still in His Neck
excerpt: Wilmer Cuscul Pivaral, 33, shot during a September traffic stop in Portland, appeared by video from Tacoma detention on crutches and in a neck brace; a judge found him ineligible for bond.
body:
• Wilmer Cuscul Pivaral, 33, of Guatemala, was shot by an ICE officer during a September 26 traffic stop in Portland; the bullet remains lodged between his C3 and C4 vertebrae and doctors say it cannot be removed, his lawyers say.
  • He appeared in immigration court on October 15 by video from detention in Tacoma, using crutches and wearing a neck brace.
  • A judge ruled him ineligible for bond after he missed the deadline to request it; his next hearing is June 16, 2026.
  • ICE says he weaponised his vehicle against officers; his lawyers say he was unarmed and are demanding his day in court and medical care.

A Guatemalan man shot by a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer during a traffic stop last month appeared in immigration court on Wednesday with the bullet still lodged in his neck, according to Oregon Public Broadcasting and KATU. Wilmer Cuscul Pivaral, 33, appeared by video from the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Washington, using crutches to walk and wearing a neck brace.

Cuscul Pivaral was shot on September 26 in Portland, Oregon, during what ICE described as a targeted traffic stop. He lives in Vancouver, Washington, with his wife and three children, the youngest eight months old, KATU reported.

A Bullet Doctors Cannot Remove

The bullet is lodged between the C3 and C4 vertebrae in his neck. His attorney, Eileen McGarry of the Inland Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, told reporters it is pressing inside his spinal cord area, that surgical removal is not possible, and that paralysis will worsen if it shifts. He needs help eating, she said.

"For him, every day is a constant struggle. Something as simple as eating is an extreme struggle."

— Eileen McGarry, attorney for Wilmer Cuscul Pivaral

An ICE spokesperson told KATU that Cuscul Pivaral receives a full health assessment within 12 hours of arrival at a facility, a comprehensive evaluation within 14 days, and round-the-clock access to medical and mental health care. His legal team is pressing for a full medical evaluation outside detention and for his release to his family.

Two Accounts of the Stop

ICE's account, given to KATU, is that Cuscul Pivaral has a criminal history, was previously arrested for illegal re-entry, weaponised his vehicle against officers during the stop, and that an officer then fired defensive shots. His lawyers dispute that version and say he was unarmed. "We want our day in court," McGarry said, arguing the shooting itself now needs to be tested in front of a judge rather than settled by agency statements.

The case has drawn in elected officials. US Representative Maxine Dexter of Oregon and Vancouver Mayor Anne McEnerny-Ogle have both spoken about it publicly, according to KATU, as immigration enforcement operations in the Portland area face growing local scrutiny.

What Happens Next

At Wednesday's hearing, the immigration judge ruled Cuscul Pivaral ineligible for bond because he had missed the deadline to apply for it, OPB reported. That leaves him in detention in Tacoma while his immigration case proceeds. His next hearing is scheduled for June 16, 2026 — an eight-month wait with, his lawyers say, a bullet in his neck and care they consider inadequate.

For now, two processes will run in parallel: the immigration case that decides whether he can stay in the United States, and the unresolved public argument over whether the shot that put him in a neck brace should ever have been fired. His full account of that September morning, OPB noted, has still not been made public.
